newsitem.title: USA: SEC says will not seek further "viatical" review.
newsitem.headline: SEC says will not seek further "viatical" review.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission said Thursday it will not petition the U.S. Supreme Court to hear a case against a Texas firm selling interests from insurance policies of AIDS victims.

The SEC had until March 20 to request a review of a U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit December decision that ruled in favor of Life Partners Inc, a Waco, Texas, firm that is in the "viatical" business.

As a viatical settlement company, the firm, the biggest player in the viatical industry, buys life insurance policies from the terminally ill at a discount and then collects the policy's full value when the insured party dies.
The SEC contended the insurance policy interests the firm sells are "securities" and therefore must register those securities with the regulatory agency.
